children: Bitcoin has had another choppy morning, initially recovering on the back of Anthropic's blockbuster Wall Street debut before backsliding a bit as investors rotate capital into Anthropic shares.

The flagship cryptocurrency was trading 0.2% higher at $62,750, up from a low of $62,086 in the previous session but retreating from a high of around $64,000 hit just ahead of the opening bell in the U.S. Ether made similar moves and sits 1.2% higher at $1,767.

Tech stock futures got a lift overnight ahead of Thursday's Anthropic debut, reversing a recent string of losses in the sector. Crypto assets tend to move in the same direction as equities, particularly tech.

That recovery stalled on Thursday morning as investors appeared to be selling stocks and crypto to make room for Anthropic shares. All three of the major indices are 0.5% or more while Anthropic's stock is up 27%.

Crypto assets are still on the mend after tumbling Wednesday when the Federal Reserve released minutes showing officials were supportive of further rate increases, and were even contemplating a half-point hike at the Fed's December meeting.

Higher interest rates make it more expensive to hold onto assets that don't provide a yield like crypto. Markets are currently pricing in a 93% chance that the Fed raises rates by a quarter-point at its next meeting, and a 7% chance of a half-point increase, according to data from CME. Odds for another hike in January sit around 73%.

"If investors expect the Fed to keep policy restrictive for longer, interest-bearing instruments could become more attractive relative to assets such as Bitcoin, whose returns depend primarily on price movements," said Simon-Peter Massabni of XS.com.

The recent selloff in AI stocks have also forced funds to cut down on their risky assets, analysts at the crypto platform Yield Basis said in a research note. "Bitcoin can be sold easily because it's so liquid," they said.
